messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Canary alert (eu-rt-3): 3.8x median token latency, tail p99->p999 spike, and kernel-fallback rate climbed to 27%. Thresholds breached at 01:04 UTC. Link: https://metrics.redwood.internal/canaries/eu-rt-3

jordan: Acknowledging. Paging eng-oncall. I'm oncall now — will triage.

aya: grabbing perf traces. Initial hypothesis: new rollout changed prefetch/batching heuristic, causing more work to hit the slow generic kernel. Seeing KV cache invalidations on some shards.

maria: which release rolled to eu-rt-3? I can roll that back if needed.

jordan: rollout id r-2026-03-15-7. Deployed ~00:50 UTC. Canary traffic was 10%.

aya: repro logs from one host:
```
[2026-03-15T01:03:12Z] kernel: selected=fallback_generic, latency=43ms, batch_size=1
[2026-03-15T01:03:12Z] runtime: prefetch_window=0.2, expected=0.6
[2026-03-15T01:03:13Z] kvcache: miss_rate=0.48
```

jordan: customer-impact check? CS, any reports?

customer-success: Not yet escalated by customers but some error-tracking spikes on high-priority accounts. CS is opening watch for any SLA hits.

sam-oncall: Are we sure this is the kernel fallback vs just higher input lengths? Any spike in seq-length distribution?

aya: checked seq lengths — stable. The changelog for r-2026-03-15-7 toggled `adaptive_prefetch = enabled` and bumped continuous-batching window to 25ms. That could increase contention and cause eviction patterns.

jordan: Plan: 1) Flip kill-flag to stop rollout to remaining canaries 2) Ramp down canary traffic on eu-rt-3 3) If that stabilizes, revert rollout. Any objections?

maria: Agreed. I'll flip the feature flag and initiate a targeted rollback if metrics don't improve in 3 mins.

jordan: Command to flip flag:
```
redwoodctl feature set runtime.adaptive_prefetch false --scope canary:r-2026-03-15-7
```

maria: running now...

dev-deploy-bot: Executing: redwoodctl feature set runtime.adaptive_prefetch false --scope canary:r-2026-03-15-7
dev-deploy-bot: Success. Flag state: disabled for canary r-2026-03-15-7.

aya: after flag flip: kernel-fallback rate down to 9% within 60s, median token latency improved ~30%. Still watching p99 tail.

jordan: good. Maria, please perform full rollback for r-2026-03-15-7 to eu-rt-3 and stop further rollouts. Use canary rollback endpoint.

maria: kicking rollback for eu-rt-3 now.

dev-deploy-bot: Rollback triggered: r-2026-03-15-7 -> previous r-2026-03-14-2 on eu-rt-3. Progress: 40% -> 80% -> 100%.

maria: rollback complete. Telemetry shows p50 returned to baseline and p99 decreasing. I'll keep a pinned graph.

customer-success: Notified top 5 affected accounts proactively: explained rollback and mitigation. No active incidents reported.

jordan: Escalation notes: probable cause = interaction between adaptive_prefetch and continuous-batching window leading to higher eviction and generic-kernel fallback. Follow-ups: 1) reproduce on staging with A/B of prefetch/window 2) add guardrail metric for kernel-fallback rate to auto-pause rollouts 3) postmortem if customers were impacted.

aya: I'll run targeted repros this morning + perf profiling. Also adding a quick safety check in the rollout controller to fail canary if fallback_rate > 10% for 2 consecutive minutes.

sam-oncall: handing off to lee-next for next shift — leaving runbook links and graphs in the thread.

lee-next: ACK. I'll watch the dashboards for the next 4 hours and coordinate with runtime team if we see reappearance.

jordan: Thanks team. Closing immediate incident. Will open follow-up ticket for postdeploy-guardrails and root-cause analysis. :white_check_mark:
